newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Christmas blues hit demand, prices soft.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Christmas blues hit demand, prices soft.

text.p: A seasonal slump in rubber demand as the Christmas holiday period approaches is likely to hit prices, while news INRO hopes to meet a deadline on a rubber pact is not causing a ripple in the market, traders said on Monday.

"With Christmas coming around soon, it's going to be quiet. The Europeans have already started on their holidays. It's very difficult finding any buyers around," a dealer for a Japanese rubber trading company said.
"Christmas and New Year holidays are coming up. Buyers are likely to be absent and the prices will be under more pressure during that time," a Thai trader added.
Dealers said news the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) hopes to meet a year-end deadline for a new price pact is likely be shrugged off by the market.

Some cited the dispute between Malaysia and Indonesia on who should fill the executive director's post in INRO as a factor which will keep traders neutral. The two countries have not ratified the International Natural Rubber Agreement 3 (INRA 3).
"It's a non-event as far as the market is concerned," a Singapore-based dealer said.

"The INRO thing between Indonesia and Malaysia remains unresolved so people will wait until the end of the month to see what happens. It will not have any immediate impact for now," a trader for a U.S.-based rubber dealing company said.
In Indonesia, benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices should stay stable in slow trade as U.S. demand is seen remaining poor, dealers said.
"It's a holiday mood. We expect to get only few fresh inquiries in the coming days," one dealer in Medan said.
Dealers said January SIR20 offer prices remained stable at 55.50-56.00 U.S. cents a kg FOB Medan, 55.25-55.75 FOB Surabaya, Padang and Palembang, 54.50-55.00 FOB Pontianak and Jambi.
They said prompt delivery latex was on offer at 2,150 rupiah a kg against the previous 2,200 rupiah in the West Java towns of Bandung and Tangerang due to weak demand.

Another Medan dealer said he expected increased sales of SIR3CV in the coming days following a stream of fresh inquiries mainly from the United States. January SIR3CV was last traded at 141 cents/kg, he said.
Malaysian traders said they expected the benchmark RSS1 and the SMR20 rubber to weaken this week due to signs consumer demand will stay soft.
"I expect the RSS1 to trade three cents down and the SMR20 about two cents down for this week," said a dealer.
The December buying price for RSS1 was at 317.50 Malaysian cents a kg at the close of the market last week, while SMR20 was at 305.50 cents.
Weak consumer demand in the Malaysian market prompted buyers to pitch for discounts, dealers said.

Producers, however, wanted to sell at higher levels as rains in the past week may hinder supplies of latex and other raw materials reaching the market, traders said. Drum latex was quoted at 237 cents a kg on Friday.
The Malaysian Meteorological Services Department said it expected this week to be as rainy as the last.
Thai rubber prices dipped slightly due to slack demand, with the pressure on prices compounded by rising supply, trade sources said.
Traders expect prices to move in a narrow range with a downward bias until the end of the year because of the holidays.
Some traders said Japan entered the market earlier last week but bought only modest amounts of rubber.
"China was absent (while) the U.S. market seemed well-covered," a Bangkok-based trader said.
"The slow demand was exacerbated by rising supplies as yields are picking up in most rubber-producing areas," he said.
The Thai benchmark RSS3 for January shipment was quoted at around US$1.23 a kg FOB Bangkok compared with the previous $1.23-$1.24 a kg.
STR20 for January shipment dipped to $1.20-$1.22 a kg FOB Bangkok from $1.23-$1.24 a kg.

Thai rubber exports during the first 10 months of 1996 slid 14.11 percent to 1.46 million tonnes from around 1.70 million tonnes in the same period in 1995, said an official at Thailand's Rubber Research Institute.
Exports in October reached about 176,000 tonnes compared with 125,529 tonnes in October 1995, the official said.
"Despite some improvement later this year, the total amount of exports during January-October were still below that of 1995 because the exports earlier this year were quite slow," she said.
(With contributions from Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia)
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
